title: A shop inventory
description:
Keep a shop's stock in a growing array of structures, driven by commands, one per line:

```
add apple 3 0.50
add pear 2 0.75
add apple 2 0.45
remove pear 1
remove kiwi 1
remove apple 9
list
total
sell
```

prints

```
Added 3 apple
Added 2 pear
Added 2 apple
Removed 1 pear
No kiwi
Only 5 apple
apple            x5    @    0.45 =     2.25
pear             x1    @    0.75 =     0.75
Total: 3.00 (2 items, 6 units)
Could not read: sell
```

| Command | Does |
|---|---|
| `add NAME QUANTITY PRICE` | adds stock. If the item exists, the quantity goes up and the price becomes the new one. Prints `Added QUANTITY NAME` |
| `remove NAME QUANTITY` | takes stock away: `Removed QUANTITY NAME`. An item whose quantity reaches 0 is deleted. Prints `No NAME` if there is no such item and `Only N NAME` if there is not enough (and changes nothing) |
| `list` | every item in **alphabetical order**, as `"%-16s x%-4d @ %7.2f = %8.2f\n"` (name, quantity, price, quantity × price), or `(empty)` |
| `total` | `Total: VALUE (N items, M units)` with the value to 2 decimals |

Names are a single word of at most 31 characters, quantities are whole numbers from 1 up, prices are not negative. Anything else - an unknown command, a missing or bad number, a name too long - prints `Could not read: ` and the line. Empty lines are skipped.
requirements: Store each item in a `struct` with its name, quantity and price.
Keep the items in an array on the heap that grows with `realloc`.
Free all the memory before the program ends (check with Memory checks on).
Write a function to find an item by name that returns its index or -1.
